head.name: @fzlt/core/diorama
head.lead: Software 3D for cutaway tabletop scenes, drawn on a 2D canvas you own. A scene is data: objects { id, shape, size, pos, rot, color, on } where on names the object it rests on (its pos is then from the parent's top centre, and it moves, tilts and sinks with it, its alpha and tint inherited). Flat-shaded convex shapes (box with a face mask, wedge, cylinder or cone, prism from an outline, group), one directional light, edge lines, blob shadows, picking. - Painter's sort by cluster → layer → depth: a cluster is a group drawn together (fixed ranks first, then far to near by its anchor), a layer orders parts inside it, and depth orders the rest. below puts the faces under a cut plane on their own layer (hulls under water). - Points (sparks, shells, smoke) and decals go into the same sort, so effects sit between faces; a pool with rank: "depth" sorts each point among the clusters by its own depth. - Limits: faces are never split, so two faces that cross each other, or a big face beside a small one at the wrong depth, can draw in the wrong order: split them into parts, or order them with clusters and layers. A face with a vertex behind the camera is dropped, not clipped. - Pools: there is no remove; add a fixed pool up front and let go of an object (a composite with its parts) with ob.off = true: its whole subtree stops drawing, shadowing, picking and costing matrix work. hidden hides the object alone (an invisible parent whose parts still show). - No allocation per draw() in the steady state (typed arrays, a merge sort into fixed buffers, shades cached as strings). No DOM of its own and no clock: call draw() from the engine's render phase (engine.add({ render: () => d.draw() })) or on your own, and resize() after a resize. Colours are #rrggbb. 2D lengths use steer's exact hypot (the builtin boxes its arguments).

sizesNote: Measured on this build: minified and gzipped with everything it imports, the way npm run size checks the budget in CI.

items.doc: Fade what stands between the eye and the targets (a chase camera in a town): each step(dt, pts) casts rays from d.eye() to every target point (pts: [x, y, z, …], world; n of them, default all) against each object's box; one in the way eases its alpha toward ghost, one the eye is inside toward 0, the rest back to 1. Returns true while anything is still fading (keep the engine awake). Writes alpha only (render side, never the sim). Boxes off the bounds of the eye and the targets are skipped; tested counts the boxes ray-tested in the last step. No allocation per step.
